findings.Quote: He had the look of a man who'd already counted his own figure and picked the next thing before he crossed the threshold. She'd done the same three days ago with Soraya, fast enough that no one saw. That was usef
findings.Note: Beat is titled 'The Mirror Crosses' for Goldberg specifically, and the purpose calls for the NRST 'forty-first name' payoff — but the excerpt cuts off before Goldberg actually states the count/payoff line ('I never read a forty-first name' is spoken but not paid off against a revealed figure). The scene ends on a Rook/Soraya comparison rather than landing Goldberg's side-crossing.
findings.Fix: Complete the beat so Goldberg's confession culminates in an explicit reckoning of the forty-first name before cutting to any Rook/Soraya parallel.

findings.Quote: Somewhere four levels up the red light hitched, dimmed, and the draw o
findings.Note: The beat requires the cost to be paid — someone hurt, the win unclean — but the prose cuts off before confirming the harvest capability actually comes down or that anyone besides Boiler is affected; as written we only get Boiler's arm injury, not confirmation of the structural/thematic payoff (twenty-one out of reach, corp's role undeniable).
findings.Fix: Complete the beat: show the manifold fully down, the twenty-one status, and a concrete marker of corp culpability left behind.

findings.Quote: the way you look at a sentence that changes the meaning of the whole page
findings.Note: Abstract meta-simile describing a look by comparing it to reading, which restates the prior clause instead of grounding it in physical action; borders on filler-profound.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical tell, e.g., 'her knuckles white on the table edge.'

findings.Quote: There's a thing people do when a man confesses clean: they reach for him, they make the room warm again, because a cold room with a confession in it is hard to sit in.
findings.Note: Universal-truth aphorism stated as narrator wisdom rather than filtered through Rook's specific observation; reads as authorial commentary inserted for weight.
findings.Fix: Ground it in Rook's concrete memory of a specific fixer doing this, cut the generalized 'thing people do' framing.

findings.Quote: the same one Soraya had built
findings.Note: The beat's stated purpose is 'Soraya Becomes Her' — Soraya giving the crew the key and completing her arc — but the entire scene as delivered is Goldberg's monologue and revelation; Soraya doesn't appear, speak, or act. The final fragment gestures at Soraya only in a dangling comparison, contradicting the beat's premise that this is her scene.
findings.Fix: Reallocate stage time so Soraya is present and active — delivering credentials or a decisive line — rather than referenced only in Goldberg's closing analogy.

findings.Quote: You're carrying a contract for a count right now, in another woman's arms. Don't stand in my gap and call yours clean.
findings.Note: aphoristic mirror-argument line that risks feeling like an author-authored thesis statement rather than something Anneke would say in the moment; borders on the pseudo-profound universal-truth register the note warns against
findings.Fix: tighten to something more specific to the ledger/rows in front of them rather than a generalized moral maxim

findings.Quote: this once he made himself the wall that lies — the wall that carries what it was never rated for and says nothing
findings.Note: The load-bearing-structure conceit tips into a pseudo-profound aphorism that strains the literal metaphor (a wall doesn't "lie," and the phrase reaches for meaning it hasn't earned).
findings.Fix: Cut the aphoristic framing; keep it physical: "he held the give shut by main force, the way you hold a door against wind."

findings.Quote: she wrote *32 confirmed*
findings.Note: Beat purpose specifies the count resolves as twenty-one, whole and complete — the motif payoff hinges on that exact number landing clean. Introducing 32 (21 + Goldberg + the unnamed woman + implied others) muddies whether the twenty-one ever actually 'comes out whole,' diluting the intended resolution.
findings.Fix: Keep the 21 as the closed, resolved count on its own; if 32 is a running total, separate it clearly so the twenty-one's completion isn't undercut by a bigger unresolved number crowning the page.

findings.Quote: That was what you paid for when you didn't want to be seen.
findings.Note: Editorializing aside that tells rather than trusts the visual detail just given.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; let the matte description stand alone.

findings.Quote: a fourth finger came down on the table edge, uninvited
findings.Note: The count motif is meant to establish Rook's discipline, but personifying the finger as acting 'uninvited' undercuts the control the beat wants to establish before she says yes deliberately.
findings.Fix: Have her notice/suppress it rather than framing it as autonomous.

findings.Quote: the silence a building makes in the quarter-second before it admits it's done
findings.Note: Purple personification of a building; slightly overwrought for a quick flashback beat.
findings.Fix: Trim to a plainer sensory beat, e.g., 'the half-second of nothing before the slab gave.'

findings.Quote: the name did quiet work
findings.Note: Vague authorial telling-phrase that asserts significance without showing it beyond the checkpoint-scan line already given.
findings.Fix: Cut the phrase; the checkpoint detail already does the work.

findings.Quote: the way food goes when nobody touches it
findings.Note: Filler truism that states the obvious without adding image or tension.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause; 'still steaming faintly' already conveys it.

findings.Quote: the building took it in its molars and let it go
findings.Note: Anthropomorphized-building imagery ('molars') is a strained personification that doesn't add precision — a stock 'the city is alive' move.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more mechanical, specific description of the Pulse tube sound.

findings.Quote: which is a worse word than dead
findings.Note: Aphoristic turn of phrase that asserts profundity without earning it through specific imagery — slightly editorializes rather than showing the horror.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a concrete detail of what 'useful' entails for a Read on the rack.

findings.Quote: her tongue moved against the inside of her teeth, like she was checking whether the hum had ever fully left them
findings.Note: A finely-written but slightly overworked gesture-as-interiority beat; borders on a stock 'small physical tic reveals deep trauma' move.
findings.Fix: Trim to a single plain gesture without the simile explaining its meaning.

findings.Quote: because the day I opened it I'd stop being a man with a useful past and become a man with a debt he couldn't pay twice
findings.Note: Neatly symmetrical aphorism-as-dialogue; sounds composed for thematic resonance rather than as something a person under pressure would say.
findings.Fix: Flatten the line into plainer, less rhetorically balanced speech.

findings.Quote: The clean cuff came all the way undone then, the planner's economy giving over to the thing it had held back four years.
findings.Note: Repeats the 'clean cuff/discipline unraveling' metaphor from earlier in the same beat almost verbatim in structure, weakening it through redundancy.
findings.Fix: Cut this restatement since the cuff image was already used minutes earlier in the same scene.

findings.Quote: the grip that never decides whether it's holding the rail up or being held up by it
findings.Note: this line actually appears in beat 12, but the parallel construction pattern of over-elaborated hand/object gestures recurs — flagging the general device here isn't applicable; no issue in beat 0 itself
findings.Fix: n/a

findings.Quote: a man listen to a building that wasn't in the room yet
findings.Note: borderline purple but mostly earns it via the mechanical detail preceding it; the phrase itself is slightly overreaching poetic abstraction for what is otherwise a grounded technical scene
findings.Fix: cut 'that wasn't in the room yet' or ground it more concretely

findings.Quote: the kind they never turned off
findings.Note: mild stock phrasing for institutional lighting, low-impact but slightly rote
findings.Fix: specify what never turning them off costs or means instead of the generic aside

findings.Quote: she'd argued herself into this back in the planning — the perimeter doesn't work on a building you go down into — and she'd been right, and being right hadn't prepared her for how it felt
findings.Note: tells the emotional beat explicitly rather than trusting the preceding physical detail (uneven breath count) to carry it; slightly redundant explanation of the theme
findings.Fix: cut the 'being right hadn't prepared her' clause, let the breath-count stand alone

findings.Quote: Helix is offering you the math
findings.Note: slightly on-the-nose thematic labeling, tips into telling the reader what kind of scene this is rather than trusting the numbers already stated
findings.Fix: cut the line, let the trade speak for itself

findings.Quote: a hard click, like a breaker thrown
findings.Note: serviceable but a familiar mechanical-sound simile
findings.Fix: specify a more particular sound tied to Vox's actual gear

findings.Quote: Anneke held still, and that was how Rook knew she'd landed it.
findings.Note: stock 'stillness as confirmation' beat, a familiar shorthand for a landed verbal blow
findings.Fix: specify a concrete physical tell instead of narrating the meta-conclusion

findings.Quote: the last fraction before the break
findings.Note: slightly generic tension-mechanics phrasing for the trigger-pull beat
findings.Fix: anchor to a more specific sensory or mechanical detail of the Reibo itself

findings.Quote: his boots set wide, and lift
findings.Note: Generic action-hero staging language undercuts the otherwise specific tactile voice of the passage.
findings.Fix: Ground it further in Boiler's specific trade vocabulary rather than generic lifting-stance description.

findings.Quote: the lake while it did the thing it always did, which was nothing
findings.Note: A whimsical-filler turn of phrase that undercuts the gravity of the scene rather than earning quiet.
findings.Fix: Cut the quip; let the stillness be described directly, e.g., "looked at the lake, flat and unchanged."

findings.Quote: the gray of a city that had been raining for weeks and was thinking about stopping but hasn't decided
findings.Note: Personifying the weather/city with indecision is a soft pathetic-fallacy flourish that doesn't add specific meaning to Rook's reckoning.
findings.Fix: Trim to a plainer image: "the gray of a city mid-rain, no end in sight."
